bib.title: DeepSeek-VL2: Mixture-of-Experts Vision-Language Models for Advanced Multimodal Understanding

read.skipped: reference list (after offset ~53746) skimmed only for lineage

question: How can an open MoE vision-language model handle high-resolution images of varying aspect ratios and run efficiently while improving on DeepSeek-VL?
hypothesis: Dynamic tiling with a single SigLIP encoder plus a DeepSeekMoE/MLA language model and better data gives similar or better accuracy with fewer activated parameters.
contributions: a dynamic, high-resolution vision encoding strategy
an optimized language model architecture (MoE with MLA) improving training and inference efficiency
a refined vision-language data construction pipeline extending to visual grounding

method.summary: LLaVA-style VLM: SigLIP-SO400M-384 encoder applied to dynamic tiles plus a global thumbnail, 2x2 pixel-shuffle and two-layer MLP adaptor, DeepSeekMoE LLM with MLA. Trained in three stages (alignment, pretraining, SFT) in three sizes (Tiny, Small, base).
method.task: vision-language pretraining and instruction tuning; evaluated on OCR, QA, math and grounding benchmarks

datasets.name: VL pretraining mix
datasets.size: approximately 800B image-text tokens (Section 4.1); training tokens 798.5B / 808.9B / 796.5B in Table 2 stage 2
datasets.source: WIT, WikiHow, 30% of OBELICS, Wanjuan (Chinese), in-house; captions re-generated by in-house captioner and scored by DeepSeek Chat; LaTeX OCR, 12M RenderedText, in-house OCR; PubTabNet, FinTabNet, Docmatix; Websight; visual prompt QA; grounding data
datasets.preprocessing: recaptioning with OCR hints, meta info and original captions; DeepSeek Chat quality filter

datasets.name: SFT mix
datasets.source: open datasets with regenerated answers plus in-house QA, OCR, document, table/chart, math, textbook, web-to-code, grounding, Chinese QA, text-only data
datasets.preprocessing: responses regenerated using question, image and OCR; poor-OCR samples removed

datasets.name: Evaluation benchmarks
datasets.split: DocVQA test, ChartQA test, InfoVQA test, TextVQA val, OCRBench, MMStar, AI2D test, MMMU val, MME sum, MMBench en/cn test, MMBench-V1.1, MMT-Bench, RealWorldQA, MathVista testmini, RefCOCO/+/g
datasets.preprocessing: for InfoVQA candidate resolutions enlarged to mn<=18

models.params: 3B total LLM, 0.57B activated LLM, 1.0B activated total

models.name: DeepSeek-VL2-Small

models.name: DeepSeek-VL2

models.name: Qwen2-VL, InternVL2, LLaVA-OV, MM1.5, Molmo, MiniCPM-V, Phi-3.5-Vision, Pixtral, Aria-MoE, DeepSeek-VL, GPT-4V, GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini-1.5-Pro

training.objective: next-token prediction loss on text tokens only; in SFT only answers and special tokens supervised, prompts masked
training.lr: Tiny 5.4e-4 / 5.4e-4 / 3.0e-5; Small 4.2e-4 / 4.2e-4 / 1.4e-5; base 4.5e-4 / 4.5e-4 / 2e-5 (stages 1/2/3); visual encoder LR multiplier 0.1
training.lr_schedule: stage 1 cosine, stage 2 step (divides LR by sqrt(10) at 50% and 75% of steps), stage 3 constant
training.precision: BF16 optimizer used for the base model only; other precision not stated
training.regularisation: gradient clip 1.0; aux loss weight 0.001 (Tiny, Small) and 0.0001 (base); expert bias correction step 0 / 0.001 / 0 for base
training.hardware: NVIDIA A100 GPUs, 8 per node, 16/33/42 nodes
training.compute: not stated as GPU-hours; only days and node counts given

other.stage_1: vision encoder and adaptor trained, LLM frozen
other.parallelism: pipeline, tensor and expert parallelism, image tile load balancing across data-parallel ranks; HAI-LLM platform

inference.prompting: dynamic tiling disabled when more than 2 images are given

parameters.candidate_resolutions: CR = {(m*384, n*384) | 1<=m,n, mn<=9}; mn<=18 for InfoVQA
parameters.tiles: 1 global thumbnail + m_i x n_i local 384x384 tiles; tile chosen to minimise padding area

metrics.name: benchmark accuracy
metrics.definition: per-benchmark standard metric (accuracy; ANLS/relaxed accuracy not specified); MME is a sum score; OCRBench reported as raw score; RefCOCO accuracy for grounding

eval.protocol: baseline numbers in tables appear taken from other reports, not stated; * marks a different setting; no seeds or significance; HAI-LLM used for evaluation; Fig 1 average over MMBench v1.1, MMStar, MMMU val, MathVista testmini, AI2D test, OCRBench/10

evidence.quote: The training of DeepSeek-VL2 was completed in 7/10/14 days using a cluster of 16/33/42 nodes, with each node equipped with 8 NVIDIA A100 GPUs.

results.claim: Dynamic tiling uses a 384x384 SigLIP encoder on tiles chosen from candidate resolutions with m*n<=9, plus one global thumbnail.
Each tile yields 729 embeddings, compressed to 196 tokens by 2x2 pixel shuffle.
results.quote: yielding 27 × 27 = 729 visual embeddings of 1152 dimensions per tile

results.claim: Dynamic tiling is disabled when more than 2 images are input.
results.quote: we disable the dynamic tiling strategy when processing multiple

results.claim: For InfoVQA evaluation the candidate resolution limit is raised to mn<=18 because of extreme aspect ratios and very large images.
DeepSeek-VL2 (4.5B activated) scores 93.3 on DocVQA test.
DeepSeek-VL2-Small (2.8B activated) scores 92.3 on DocVQA.
DeepSeek-VL2-Tiny (1.0B activated) scores 88.9 DocVQA and 809 OCRBench.
DeepSeek-VL2 scores 78.1 on InfoVQA, the benchmark with extreme aspect ratios (Claude 3.5 Sonnet 74.1, Qwen2-VL-7B 76.5).
Qwen2-VL-7B beats DeepSeek-VL2 on DocVQA (94.5 vs 93.3) and OCRBench (845 vs 811) with 8.3B params.
DeepSeek-VL2 scores 86.0 ChartQA and 84.2 TextVQA.
DeepSeek-VL2 scores 61.3 MMStar, 51.1 MMMU val, 62.8 MathVista testmini.
DeepSeek-VL2-Small scores 57.0 MMStar.
DeepSeek-VL2-Tiny scores 45.9 MMStar with 1.0B activated.
DeepSeek-VL2 scores 95.1 RefCOCO val.

results.claim: Text vs mixed ratio in pretraining is about 70% VL to 30% text.
Concise responses worked better than detailed reasoning for the Tiny model (qualitative, no number). Text: 'DeepSeek-VL2-Tiny shows better performance with more concise responses.'

limits: Context window only allows a few images per chat session
Model occasionally struggles with blurry images or unseen objects
Reasoning capability is weaker than perception; authors plan to strengthen it
No ablation of dynamic tiling vs the old hybrid encoder; the improvement over DeepSeek-VL is shown only through end-to-end benchmark comparisons that also change LLM and data
Baseline figures appear to be copied from other reports; evaluation settings (decoding, prompts) not given
No warmup, seed, step count, decoding settings or in-house data details; in-house data not released
Qwen2-VL-7B and others beat it on some OCR and general benchmarks (e.g. DocVQA 94.5, OCRBench 845)
Tiling is disabled for more than 2 images, so multi-image inputs lose the high-resolution path
